s1.syndrome_frame: febrile skin lesions with neutropenia and recent chemotherapy
salient_findings: tender annular erythematous plaques on the neck and trunk
purpura and erythematous edematous ring on the right chest
key_facts: recent first cycle of chemotherapy (ixazomib, lenalidomide, and dexamethasone) for disease recurrence
skin biopsy showed inflammatory infiltrate of predominantly mononuclear cells
immunohistochemistry: positive for CD68 and myeloperoxidase, negative for CD138
nuclear dust present without obvious leukocytoclastic vasculitis

shortlist.label: Leukemia cutis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of multiple myeloma and recent chemotherapy, and skin biopsy showed inflammatory infiltrate of predominantly mononuclear cells with positive immunohistochemistry for CD68 and myeloperoxidase

shortlist.label: Sweet syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presents with febrile skin lesions and neutropenia, which are characteristic of Sweet syndrome, and recent chemotherapy is a known trigger

shortlist.label: Neutrophilic eccrine hidradenitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has neutropenia and recent chemotherapy, which are risk factors for neutrophilic eccrine hidradenitis, and skin lesions are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Ecthyma gangrenosum
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has neutropenia and recent chemotherapy, which are risk factors for ecthyma gangrenosum, and skin lesions are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Pyoderma gangrenosum
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presents with febrile skin lesions and recent chemotherapy, which are characteristic of pyoderma gangrenosum, and skin biopsy showed inflammatory infiltrate of predominantly mononuclear cells

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of fever, tender skin lesions, and laboratory findings such as elevated C-reactive protein and negative blood culture, along with the skin biopsy showing an inflammatory infiltrate of predominantly mononuclear cells, are consistent with Sweet syndrome. The patient's recent chemotherapy and neutropenia also support this diagnosis, as Sweet syndrome can be associated with neutropenia and is often seen in patients with underlying hematologic malignancies.

rejected.label: Leukemia cutis
rejected.why: The immunohistochemistry results were negative for CD138, which is more commonly associated with multiple myeloma, and the presence of myeloperoxidase-positive cells does not necessarily indicate leukemia cutis in this context.

rejected.label: Neutrophilic eccrine hidradenitis
rejected.why: This condition is more commonly associated with neutropenia and fever but typically involves the eccrine glands, which was not specifically noted in the skin biopsy findings.

rejected.label: Ecthyma gangrenosum
rejected.why: This condition is typically associated with Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection, which was not indicated by the negative blood culture or the clinical presentation.

rejected.label: Pyoderma gangrenosum
rejected.why: While this condition can present with similar skin lesions, the overall clinical picture and laboratory findings do not align as closely with pyoderma gangrenosum as they do with Sweet syndrome.
